burial: Lamp. Across Seven Flags, the oldest person in every house lights the first lantern.
The sun takes him at first light, mija. By summer he'll be clean bone.
Everybody hates the sun. It takes us anyway.
Señor, Elías kept his family in his hands. Keep him in Yours. Amén.
Your mamá left this on the counter before she went. It's yours now.
Eleven days, Juno. Don't you go doing anything stupid.
Like doing it alone. Go feed your goats. They don't know anybody died.

n2_table: Sit, mija. The table's for everybody. Tonight it's for you.
Every family owes the town a share. Water, salvage, a watch on the wall. That's how there's still a town.
The water shift, with Fina. And his salvage route, out to the Big Store.
Now it's yours. Nobody at this table thinks you can't.
And get yourself wraps before you need them. Rubén has some. The white doesn't wait to see if you're ready.
n7_meeting: Under the seven flags, the whole town. Everybody talking at once.
Halogen's been asking up and down the Thirty-Five about something. He calls it the Cold.
So give it to his riders, and they leave us alone.
Riders don't leave anybody alone. Smash it, and the machines stop coming.
Smash it, and what if it was the one good thing?

n7_meeting.q: They're all looking at the canister in Juno's arms.
opts: If we trade it, the riders go.
If we break it, the machines stop.

n7_meeting: It isn't ours to break, and it isn't ours to sell.
The screen on the canister lights up, and NIM speaks, loud enough for the whole Plaza.
Hello. My name is NIM. I'm a seed. For the sky.
If somebody gets me to the right place, I can make it rain.
...Applause. Your papá said it sounds like applause.
n7_goodbyes: Your papá's wraps. Mirror cloth. He walked to San Antonio in these once, and back.
Keep the lantern lit, mija. Somebody always has to.
Me. Until you're back. Go and find Kit. He's at the Ramp, talking to a sign.
night:7: Go on. I'm too old to watch anybody walk away twice in one night.
home: I'll sit with him till Shutter. Go on. Those goats are yelling at you.
market: Chayo was asking for you. The Plaza, west down the boulevard. Take the milk.
*: Keep the lantern lit, mija. Somebody always has to.

home&!fed: The goats crowd the gate, yelling like it's the end of the world.
It is the end of the world. Eat your mesquite.
*: The goats are busy ignoring you. Pancha's spot by the gate is empty.

home&!tank: The tank is half full. Papá's dew lines held another night.
Fill up before you go. Mamá always said that.

homeDone: Two jars of milk. Doña Chayo will trade for that.
platform: Your father, wrapped in white. At first light, the sun takes him.

n2_table: Sit by me. Lupe goes first, then Memo goes longer.
market: Ay, Juno. Come here, come here. Let me look at you.
You look like your papá. That's not a compliment. He always looked tired.
Milk! Okay. Two jars of milk is worth...
...two tins of white. And don't argue, I know what you're going to say.
That's what I said you'd say. Take two. Your mamá never once sold me gray.
Now go find that Kit before he talks somebody to death. He's been asking for you all night.

opts: Marta said to say thank you.
Hm. Same sack next week. Don't make a face about it.
Good. Now don't stand there. You're blocking my light.

q_flour&!flour_given: Up the Old Trail. Follow the lanterns. Marta. Go.
sides&!q_flour: Juno. You're walking around anyway. Walk somewhere useful.
Up the Old Trail, past the last yards, there's a church on the hill. Lanterns all the way.
Take this up to Marta. Don't open it, don't sell it, and don't tell anybody where you're going.
flour_thanked: Eleven years nobody said a word to me about it. Then you.
...Go on. Your face is still going to burn, white or no white.
night:7&!chayo_bye: Your mamá never once sold me gray. Don't you start out there.
night:7: Go on. Before I cry in front of the whole market.
*: White's not for looking at, mija. Put it on before you leave, not when you feel it.

n2_shares&has:salve&!salve_used: What? My hand's fine. It's a normal amount of blood.

n2_shares&has:salve&!salve_used.q: Use Fina's salve on Kit's hand?
opts: Juno opens the tin and works the salve into the cut. Kit narrates every second of it.
Okay. Okay. That's cold. That's so cold. I'm being very brave about this, write that down.

n2_shares&!salve_used: Fina's going to make you carry water to every house in town. I'll supervise.
night:6: Lake. Wreck. Not dying. That's the plan, right? I like the not dying part.
night:7: I packed. I packed twice. Pancha's staying with my tía. She's not happy about it.
kit: Does rain make a noise? Like, when it hits stuff?
Kit, I've never seen rain. Nobody has.
Your papá said his abuelo heard it once. He said it sounds like applause.
She went down toward the drain, east of the park. There's something down there, Juno. It's got a light.
pancha: East of the park. The drain. Please, Juno?
*: Does Pancha count as a party member? I think she counts.

n2_shares&!wraps_got&white:1: Wraps. Your papá's size, nearly. One tin.

n2_shares&!wraps_got&white:1.q: Daylight wraps for one tin of white?
opts: Cloth for going out in the white. Face, hands, neck. Leave nothing out.
They won't save you. They'll buy you a little time. That's all anything buys.

n2_shares&!wraps_got: No tin? Your papá's credit is still good at this stall. Take them.
Cloth for going out in the white. Face, hands, neck. Leave nothing out.
neto_met&!q_neto_done: He's alive. He drank the water.

neto_met&!q_neto_done.q: Neto asked you not to say where he sleeps.
opts: He's at the long roof. In the middle, where the fountain is.
...Then I know where to leave water. He'll know the knots on the jug.
He's alive. That's all he'd let me say.
That's more than I had this morning.

q_neto&!neto_met: South-west. The long roof. He'll be where the roof's still on.
sides&!q_neto: You're going out past the edges now. I've seen you.
My brother, Neto. He went south-west, to the long roof. Three months ago. He doesn't come back.
He sold white that wasn't. Cut with chalk. They were going to send him to noon.
Take him this. Tell him... no. Just take it.
neto_told: I leave a jug by the broken doors every week. It's gone in the morning.
He never leaves a note. He never could write.
neto_kept: Seven flags. Seven nations owned this ground once, they say.
He's alive. I keep saying it to myself. It's a good sentence.
*: Seven flags. Seven nations owned this ground once, they say.
Can't name a single one of them. Doesn't matter. They're gone, and we're still here.

n5_market: Sit. The market's slow tonight. Everybody's looking east.
You know what my abuela used to say? Before things change, the dogs leave.
The dogs in the Big Store were gone.
...Then go home and look at the sky a while. With people you like.
night:7: My abuela would tell you: if you hear La Llorona out on the road, you don't look.
Then you look. You look as long as you want.
n2_table: Shares, mija. Everybody carries something. Even me. Mostly stories.
*: You hear her last night? La Llorona. Down in the Dead River.
My abuela said if you hear her crying, you don't go look. You don't help. You go home.
Did your abuela ever go look?

tavo: Did you know the Old Trail is the oldest place in the whole world?
Abuelo Nacho says the first people walked it. It's north. It has benches.
nacho: Careful, mija. You're walking on history.
It's the oldest trail in the world. The first families walked it to get here.
There's a bench up the way. Somebody carved a heart in it. Ancient.
bench: Someone carved a heart into the old bench, a very long time ago.
well: The bucket comes up wet. Somebody's lucky night.
drainIntro: Pancha is backed against the concrete, bleating.
Something rolls out of the culvert's dark mouth. Six wheels. One red eye.
That's a Stray. That's a Stray, Juno.
A coyote slinks in behind it, following the noise. Following the meal.
Then pretend it's a bird with one eye.
drainWin: The Stray shudders and goes still. Its eye fades to nothing.
You hit it in the eye. Like your papá's book says.
Mamá's book. Papá just wrote in it louder.
Can I come with you? Like, from now on? On everything?
That's a yes. I'm counting that as a yes.
Shutter's coming. Let's get home before the sky goes white.
fall: Juno. Juno, wake up. Come look.
Kit, it's day. Get inside before you go white.
Everybody's up on the roofs. Look up.
Nothing comes down from up there. Nothing ever comes down.
faint: The white closes in. Your hands stop working right. You've stopped sweating.
Someone drags you under a roof. You wake at Mar Farm, the next Lamp, with one less tin of white.

n2_shares&!fina_started: Your papá's shift. Two jugs, mija. One down to the Cellars, one to Toña at the Chapel table.
Rooms dug under the old houses. Thirty, fifty feet down, cool all day. Inés's hatch is the one with the blue lantern, behind the Plaza.
n2_shares&fina_started&!fina_done&drop_c: Both? And you didn't drink one. Your papá always drank one.
Here. For the kid's hand. I saw him hiding it.
n2_shares&fina_started&!fina_done: One down the Cellars, one to Toña. Go on, the water's not getting colder.
night:7: Clean, boiled, blessed. All three, for once. For the road.
*: Agua, agua. Clean, boiled, blessed. Two out of three, guaranteed.

n2_memo: Riders on the Thirty-Five last night. Halogen's colors.
The big road north. Goes all the way to the cold, they say.
Riders don't come down it for nothing. Bar your door tonight.
n3_tithe: Two riders stand at the barricade in white quilted suits and mirrored visors, tubes running into their collars.
They ride at noon. That's the whole point. Showing you they can.
The tithe. Water, from every town on the Thirty-Five. Every month, every town.
Memo hands over four jugs. Nobody speaks. One rider's visor stays turned toward Juno a beat too long.

opts: Juno says nothing. The visor turns away.
The rider says it like something to remember.

n3_tithe: They go west at a walk, in no hurry. Nobody moves until they're gone.
Go home, mija. Don't be out when the bell goes.
n4_memo: In the dust past the barricade: tracks. Hundreds. Six wheels, treads, things with feet. All going one way.
East. Every machine in the brush, heading for the White Bowl.
The White Bowl. There was a lake there once, my abuelo said. You couldn't see across it.
Something out there is calling them. Don't you go and answer it.
n6_east: East road's sealed. Nobody goes to the lake.
...I didn't see you. I didn't see the kid either.
night:7: Rafa did the straps on that pack. I did the hard part. Supervising.
Thirty-Five north. Chuy will let you by. Don't stop for riders.
n2_table: Talk to Lupe. She runs the table, whatever she tells you.
pancha: Drain's east of the park. If that's where you're going, take a pipe.
Something's been rolling around out there at night. Little tracks. Six wheels.
home2: Heard the noise from here. You and the kid okay?
Then get home. Shutter waits for nobody.
*: Nobody goes out the east road after Lamp. Not without a reason and a pipe.
Big tracks out by the lake lately. Bigger than any Stray.

n4_mower: It stopped at Shutter. Right in the middle of a row.
The little mower sits in its square of dead grass, still. It's turned to face east.
They're all facing east. The Strays went east. Everything's going east.
night:7: Then push me on the swing when you do. Higher than Tavo.
*: Tavo says the Old Trail is the oldest place in the world. I say it's the drain.
The drain has bones in it. That's how you know it's old.

n2_shares&fina_started&!drop_tona: Fina's water. Bless her, and bless you for carrying it.
One candle for Elías. One for Rosa, in case. And one for whoever's walking tonight.
n4_shoes&has:shoes: His shoes. Ay, look at the heels. He walked crooked, your papá.
Toña sets the shoes under the candles, toes pointing out, the way you leave shoes by a door.
So he walks easy. Wherever he's walking.
n4_shoes&shoes_asked: His shoes, mija. They'll be by his chair.
n4_shoes: Juno. Bring me Elías's shoes. For the shrine.
The dead walk a long way. Nobody should do it barefoot.
night:7&shoes_given: His shoes are under the candles. He walks easy. Now you.
One for whoever's walking tonight. That's you, mija. It was always going to be you.
night:7: One candle for whoever's walking tonight. I'll keep it lit till you're back.
*: One candle for Elías. One for Rosa, in case.
And one for whoever's walking tonight. That's you, mija. Go on. I've got you covered.

intro: Again? You know it better than I do.
The whole thing. Don't skip the machines.
...Okay. Okay. Come closer to the fire.
A long time ago, the sky was full. Clouds, white and gray, big as mountains.
And when they got heavy, water fell out of them. All by itself. For free.
For free? Not even a tin?
Not even a tin. It fell on the roofs and the roads and the dogs. People ran from it.
Then the world got hot. Hotter every year. Whole towns packed up and walked north, looking for shade.
So the people built machines. Six hundred of them. And they sent them up to cool the sky down.
They sprayed it with a kind of dust. A shade, to hide us from the sun.
And it worked. For a few years it was cool again. Everybody said we'd been saved.
But something lived up there, mija. Something nobody knew about. Smaller than dust.
It was what made the clouds. And the machines' dust was killing it.
One lady did. A doctor. She wrote it all down, and nobody listened.
Then the clouds got thin, and the water got scarce, and people went to war over what was left.
Somebody blew up the stations that told the machines what to do. And the spraying stopped.
When the machines finally stopped, the heat came all at once. The sky turned white.
They called it the White Year. It lasted the rest of their lives.
She asked for the whole thing.
Most people didn't make it. The ones who did went down. Under bridges. Under stores. Into the dark, where the lanterns are.
They learned to sleep through the day and wake up when the sun goes down. Like us.
And up top, the machines kept going. They still walk the day, doing whatever they were told a hundred years ago.
Some people say something is still up there. Circling. Waiting for somebody to tell it what to do.
The part where water fell out of the sky.
Your papá's abuelo swore he heard it once, when he was little. He said it sounded like applause.
That's why we never walk in white, Juno. The day belongs to the sun.
Papá... will it ever rain again?

n2_sleep: Before she sleeps, Juno opens the staybook and writes in it, in her own hand, for the first time.
n3_late: Juno lies down. Far off, the bell starts. Then, under it, someone pounding on the hatch.
n3_search|n3_home: Not now. Not with Güero out there.
*: Her cot, in the cooler, beside their bed.

shutterBell: Far off to the east, a bell starts ringing.
First light. Doors seal. Anyone still outside when the bell stops is on their own.
So I'm going to run. Come on, Pancha. See you at Lamp, Juno.
emptyChair: Papá's chair, still facing the door.
Juno sits beside it a while.
Under the door, the light turns white.

q_flour&!flour_given: Is that Chayo's sack? Ay, gracias, mija. Set it down here, before your arms fall off.
Every week for eleven years. She has never once walked up here herself.
She said not to tell anybody.
She told us if we ever thanked her in town, she'd stop. So we don't. We thank God for her instead. She can't make Him stop.
The bread on the table inside is hers. Go eat some. Sitting down.
flour_given: Chayo's bread is on the table inside. Don't tell her it's good. She knows.
Water's free. Sit down before you drink it.
*: Water's free, mija. Sit down before you drink it.
Nobody drinks standing up here. That's the only rule I make.

bell_got&!bell_hung: That's it. That's the bell. That's our bell.
I'll get it up in the arch before Lamp. Pastor's going to pretend he isn't crying.
q_bell&!bell_got: The long roof. South-west of town, down the side street past the last yards. Scavengers sleep in there.
bell_hung: It rings at Lamp now. Every Lamp. I pull the rope, and everybody on the hill stops for a second.
Pastor says that's the whole point.
*: The windmill down the trail fills the tank. I fill the jugs. Marta fills the cups.
See the arch up on top of the front? There was a bell in it once.
They rang it for every baby born and every one given to the sun. Somebody took it down for the brass, before I was born.
Scavengers say there's a bell down at the long roof, south-west of town. If it's ours... I can't go. Somebody has to carry the water.

bell_hung: Benny rang it at Lamp. Marta cried, and says she didn't.
I don't know who hung it the first time. I know who they rang it for. Same as us.
*: Come in out of it. Nobody here is going to ask you for anything.
We don't know much about the people who built this place. We know they fed whoever came up the road, and we know who they did it for.
So we keep doing it. That's most of what I preach.

q_neto&!neto_met: He ties the cap the same way. Since we were kids.
It was one batch. Kids were burning. Real white cost three tins. I made it cost one.
Half chalk still beats nothing on your face. Mostly.
Don't tell him where I sleep. If he knows, he'll come. If he comes, somebody follows him.
q_bell&!bell_got: There's a bell. Brass. It belongs to the church on the hill.
The bell. Yeah. Pawn shop, behind a grille somebody already broke. Heavy.
Brass is worth something. Two tins of white and it's yours.

q_bell&!bell_got.q: Two tins of white for the bell?
opts: Everything in here was somebody's. Two tins.

neto_told: Somebody leaves a jug by the doors every week. No note.
neto_kept: Good. Tell nobody anything. You're good at it.
neto_met: Go tell him I'm alive. Just that. Nothing about where.
shop_done: Did it say welcome? It says welcome to me through the grille. Every night.
*: Don't touch the pack. Anything else in here, take it if you can find it.
Grilles are down on all of it. Except that one. I don't go in that one.

bell_got: Careful with it. It rings if you look at it wrong.
*: Two tins. The bell's not going anywhere. Neither am I.

shop_done: The grille, up a hand's width off the floor. Light under it.
*: One grille stops a hand's width off the floor. Beyond it, light. Somebody kept the lights on.

opts: Juno lies flat and pulls herself through on her elbows.

shop_done: Welcome! Let me know if you need help finding anything.
*: Shelves of toys, every one set out in a perfect row. Dust on everything but the toys.
Welcome! Let me know if you need help finding anything.
We have a special today. For the little ones.
Welcome! Let me know if you need help finding anything.
It lifts something off the nearest shelf and holds it out. A small stuffed cloud, gray, with three blue felt drops sewn underneath. The tag says ages 3 and up.

*.q: The machine holds out the cloud.
opts: Thank you for shopping with us! Come back soon!
Juno sets the cloud back on the shelf. The machine moves it a finger's width, so the row is straight again.
Welcome! Let me know if you need help finding anything.

wake2: Lamp. Somebody is pounding on the door.
Juno! You slept through Daysleep like a dead man.
Daysleep's for sleeping, Kit. That's the whole word.
The elders want you. At the Chapel. Hermana Lupe said bring you, so I'm bringing you.

n2_shares&fina_started&!drop_cellar: Fina's water? Gracias, mija. Set it by the steps, the floor's cooler.
Is that Juno Mar? Kit says you killed a Stray with your face.
n4_ines&guero_lost: Doña Inés sits on the bottom step of the cellar, facing the hatch. She doesn't look up.
He'll be thirsty. When he comes back.

n4_ines&guero_lost.q: The lantern by her hatch has gone out.
opts: Juno goes up and lights the lantern by the hatch, and leaves it where Inés can see it from the steps.
Juno leaves the water she brought on the step, and goes up quietly.

n4_ines: You walked into the white for him. Nobody does that. Nobody.
She presses a tin of white into Juno's hands. It's half full.
I saw where they went. The machines. They all went to the lake.
They're waiting there. All of them.
night:7&guero_lost: If you see him out there. On the road.
night:7: I want to go with you. I can carry stuff. I carried a whole jug once.
He's staying. Go with God, mija. Come back with rain.
*: Mind your head on the way down. Everybody hits it once.

n3_search: Juno? I followed them. They went in a line. Like a parade.
Güero. Your mamá is going out of her mind.
They're all going to the lake. All of them. Like something's calling.
Up. Hold my hand. Shade to shade, and you don't let go.
night:4: Mamá says I can't go outside until I'm forty.
*: Kit says you killed a Stray with your face.

dogs: Something moves between the shelves at the back. Low, and more than one.
dogsWin: The last dog limps off into the dark. The biggest one wore a collar, rotted through.
Somebody had that dog once. Somebody loved it.
Somebody loved all of them once.

n2_store&dogs_done: High on the end of an aisle, chalk on the metal: E.H., in Papá's hand. A tick for every shelf he cleared.
n2_store: Shelves to the roof. Something is breathing at the back of the store.
n5_shelves: Give me a boost. No, a real boost.
Kit climbs. Juno climbs after him. The last two shelves: a roll of Papá's tools, still oiled, and a coil of mirror wire.
Juno chalks a tick on each. Under E.H., she writes J.M.
*: Papá's chalk: E.H., and a tick on every shelf.

wake3: Lamp. Kit is at the door, out of breath, pointing.
Juno. The Strays. You have to see. Come on!
They never do that. They never go in a line. They never go anywhere.
I'm so happy and I'm going to throw up.
Far off, at the east barricade, voices. Strangers' voices.
gueroGone: Güero. He went after the machines. East. He said he wanted to see where they go.
Outside, the sky is going white.
The white. Every step in the sun costs water; shade only slows it. Find him, and get you both home.
reunion: Inés doesn't let go of her son for a long time.
Mamá. Mamá, they're all at the lake. All the machines. Like they're waiting.
Juno. I can't... Go home, mija. Sleep. Go before the white takes you too.
gueroLost: The white closes in. The last thing Juno sees is the sky, and nothing in it.
She wakes in the cooler at Lamp. Memo dragged her in at dusk.
You were alone, mija. There was nobody with you.
Güero's small footprints lead east, after the machines, until the wind takes them.
gueroDragged: The white closes in, Güero's hand still in hers.
She wakes in the cooler at Lamp. Memo dragged them both in at dusk.
The boy was sitting on you. Keeping the sun off your face with his shirt.

guero_lost: Lamp. Kit is at the door. He doesn't knock.
Nina says the mower stopped. In Abby's yard. It just stopped.
*: Lamp. Kit is at the door, and for once he knocks.
Güero's telling everybody you carried him home on your back through the white. Is that true?
I'm telling it the back way.
Also Nina says the mower stopped. In Abby's yard. It just stopped.

n4_shoes&shoes_asked&!has:shoes&!shoes_g: Papá's shoes, by his chair. Still laced the way he left them.
shoes_given: The place by his chair where his shoes were.
*: Papá's shoes, by his chair. Still laced the way he left them.

wake5: Lamp. The town sounds the way it always does. That's almost strange now.
Your papá's two shelves. Tonight? We should do it tonight.
I don't know. It feels like a tonight.

n5_roof: A ladder up the side of the store. Kit is already halfway up.
On the roof the town is all lanterns, and past it the brush is all dark.
Out at the White Bowl: lights. Small and many, moving slow, like a fair.
That's them. That's all the machines.
Do you think rain is loud? Like, loud loud?
n7_roof: The roof. The lanterns. NIM's screen lights the underside of Juno's chin.
There's a place called Station Nine. North. Far.
A lake so big you can't see across it. If I get there, I can grow a sky.
Juno remembers a sheet, a fire, her father's hands making birds.

n7_roof.q: Nobody is going to make her.
opts: Juno sits a while longer. The lanterns burn.

*: A ladder up the side of Mar Farm. The roof is where the town watches the sky.

wake6: Lamp. Kit is at the door with a pipe and a water jug, which he holds up like an answer.
Memo sealed the east road. Nobody goes to the lake. Everybody's saying it.
You're going. I can tell. You've got your going face.
I'm coming. I'm not asking, I'm telling you a thing that's happening.

n6_wreck: The drone lies across the lakebed, longer than the store, its skin split open. Scavengers from town pry at it with bars.
Don't touch the edges. They're hot even at night.
There's a hatch on the far side, hanging open. Nobody wants to go first.
Up on the dam, two figures in white quilted suits stand very still, watching.

scout: The visor doesn't move. It's watching the wreck.

n6_wreck: A hatch, hanging open. Inside, something hums.
Maybe ask the ones with the bars first?

plane: An old plane with propellers, sunk in the crust to its wings. It's been here longer than anybody.
footprint: In a patch of mud the wind didn't reach: a small footprint. Just one.

n6_fuselage: At the end of the tilted corridor, in a cradle of cold metal: a canister the size of a water jug, frost on its sides.
Juno pulls it free. It's heavier than it looks, and cold enough to hurt.
A small screen on its side lights up. Two dots, and a line under them. A face.
Oh! Hello! Hello. Can you tell me what day it is?
Oh. Oh, that's a lot of years.
Did it work? Did anyone launch the others?
Outside, through the hull, something enormous starts to climb.
Oh no. I'm talking too much. When I talk, they hear me. The Wardens. They answer each other.

wardenRise: Over the lip of the dam, something climbs: four legs, a dome, one white eye.
That's a Warden. It heard me. I'm sorry. I'm sorry!
wardenWin: The Warden's eye goes dark, and the whole machine settles into the crust like something tired.
I'll be quiet. I'll try. The quieter I am, the weaker they hear me.
Up on the dam, the two figures in white turn and walk west, not hurrying.
wake7: Noon. Memo's bell, in the middle of Daysleep. It doesn't stop.
Juno! Juno, the machines! They're all around the farm!
Through the crack of the door: Strays, circling the lot in the white. Out past the yards, Hounds pace the brush, low and fast.
Hounds. Memo says they're Hounds. They hunt.
They can hear me, even when I'm quiet. I'm sorry.
Then we wait for Lamp. Nobody opens a door.
